title: Anthropic has signed a $35bn cloud deal with Nvidia-backed Lambda
content:
Anthropic has committed $35bn to a cloud provider most people have never heard of, for capacity in a Texas data centre being built by a former bitcoin miner.
The Wall Street Journal reported the Lambda agreement on Monday, and Reuters confirmed it with a person familiar with the matter.
Neither company has announced it, and no term was disclosed. We have not independently verified the report, which rests on unnamed sources.
Lambda is backed by Nvidia, and the structure around the deal is where it gets interesting. Lambda holds the lease on a data centre in Nueces County, Texas, developed by Hut 8, while Nvidia has a separate arrangement with Hut 8 to secure the capacity, and Lambda deploys Nvidia chips into it.
Follow that chain, and Nvidia appears at three points in a transaction it is not formally party to. It has invested in the tenant, contracted for the site, and supplies the hardware that fills it.
The chipmaker has been building exactly this apparatus all year, helping cloud providers secure the financing and property they need to deploy its systems.
It is the same logic behind the revenue-sharing programme it introduced in July and paused last week after internal antitrust concerns.
For Anthropic, the deal is one of several very large numbers signed in quick succession. It agreed to spend $45bn over six years with Nscale for capacity in West Virginia earlier the same month.
Amazon has separately said Anthropic will spend more than $100bn on AWS over the next decade, for five gigawatts of capacity and access to Trainium3 silicon. Set against that, $35bn is not the largest commitment on the list.
The pattern is by now well established. Anthropic signed a $9.1bn, 20-year deal with bitcoin miner Riot Platforms, a $10bn arrangement with a week-old cloud startup, and a larger package with Google and Broadcom.
Anthropic has also been in early talks to lease $10bn of compute from Meta, which is an unusual conversation between two companies that compete for the same engineers and the same enterprise budgets.
What links them is a preference for many suppliers over one. A company whose product is a single model family has an obvious interest in not depending on a single provider of the compute that runs it.
There is a concentration question underneath the diversification. Spreading contracts across many providers looks like resilience until you notice that most of them are deploying the same vendor’s chips in buildings that vendor helped secure.
Bitcoin miners keep appearing in these deals for unglamorous reasons. They hold grid connections, land and power contracts that took years to assemble, which are now the scarcest inputs in the industry and considerably harder to acquire than chips.
Hut 8 is the second miner-turned-operator in Anthropic’s supply chain after Riot. The conversion of crypto infrastructure into AI infrastructure has been one of the quieter structural shifts of the past two years.
Texas is doing a lot of work in these announcements too. Cheap land, a separate grid and a permitting regime that moves faster than most have made it the default answer for anyone who needs a gigawatt in a hurry.
None of these commitments is a cost that has already been incurred. They are multi-year obligations against revenue that has been growing quickly but has not yet reached the scale the contracts assume.
Anthropic’s run rate has been rising fast enough to make the arithmetic defensible, having passed $30bn earlier in the year. Whether it reaches the level these contracts assume is a different question from whether it is growing.
That is the bet in every one of them. Anthropic is contracting now for the capacity it will need if demand continues, at prices agreed before anyone knows whether it will.

report.summary: Anthropic向Lambda签350亿美元云合同，Nvidia幕后布局。
report.background: Anthropic作为头部AI公司，为满足快速增长的大模型训练与推理需求，正在大规模锁定算力资源。此次与Lambda的350亿美元合同是其一连串巨额采购中的最新一环，此前已与Nscale、AWS等签署数百亿乃至千亿美元级协议。Lambda是一家获得Nvidia投资的小型云服务商，租用前比特币矿工Hut 8在德州建设的数据中心，而Nvidia则通过投资、签约和供应芯片等方式深度介入。该交易反映了AI算力市场的新结构：比特币矿工凭借电网和土地转型为数据中心运营商，德州因地利成为选址热门，Nvidia则通过间接手段巩固其硬件主导地位。
key_points: Anthropic承诺向Lambda投入350亿美元，用于租用德州一座由前比特币矿工Hut 8开发的数据中心，交易尚待正式公布。
Nvidia虽未直接签约，但通过投资Lambda、与Hut 8签订容量协议、供应GPU芯片，在交易中扮演三重角色，凸显其市场掌控力。
这是Anthropic分散算力供应商策略的一部分，其近期还投资Nscale、AWS、Riot等，累计承诺超千亿美元，避免单一依赖。
表面多元化的供应商大多仍使用Nvidia芯片，并借助Nvidia协助获取融资和场地，实际集中度风险依然存在。
比特币矿工因握有电网接入、土地和电力合同等稀缺资源，正成为AI数据中心的关键供给方，转型趋势加速。
report.impact: 此交易对AI行业意味着算力军备竞赛进一步加剧，Nvidia通过间接方式强化了硬件生态的主导地位，中小云服务商则借助资本和物业资源获得发展机会。对开发者而言，Anthropic获得更多算力后，其模型服务可能更稳定，但大量长期合同带来的成本压力或间接体现为API价格波动。对普通用户，AI产品可用性有望提升，但行业高额基建投入也可能导致服务捆绑或数据依赖加深。
report.tools: 可关注Anthropic的Claude API进行应用开发；Lambda的GPU云平台提供按需算力；Nvidia的DGX系统用于自建基础设施；开源推理工具如vLLM可帮助优化模型部署成本。
